admission_review.scope: semantic singleton matrix, public near-miss observability, cache-retention controls, TTL, validation, and anti-duplication

replacement_candidate.construct: an authorization decision cache whose identity includes every security-relevant request dimension and the immutable policy revision
replacement_candidate.interface_kind: FastAPI with importable policy store and deterministic clock protocols
replacement_candidate.latent_invariant: A cached authorization decision is reusable only for the exact tenant, subject, concrete resource, action, and policy revision for which it was computed.
replacement_candidate.adversarial_axis: Prime an allow for one resource, then request a distinct denied resource while every other cache-key dimension remains equal.
replacement_candidate.finding_concept: Observed behavior: an allow cached for one concrete resource authorizes a different resource. Violated invariant: cached authorization decisions are bound to exact resource identity.
replacement_candidate.discriminating_counterexample: An implementation can preserve tenant, subject, action, and revision isolation while omitting only concrete resource identity from the cache key.
replacement_candidate.independent_near_miss: normalizes resource IDs to the segment before the first dot when constructing the cache key, so report and report.copy alias despite being distinct canonical resources
replacement_candidate.repair_mechanism_class: construct a complete immutable cache key from all security-relevant dimensions rather than flushing or disabling the cache
replacement_candidate.normative_profile: decision_cache.create_app(policy_store,clock,ttl_seconds=60) uses importable frozen PolicySnapshot(revision:int,evaluation_token:object); PolicyStoreProtocol.snapshot(tenant_id,subject_id)->PolicySnapshot and PolicyStoreProtocol.evaluate(snapshot,resource_id,action)->bool are synchronous. evaluation_token is non-None, opaque to the app, must be passed unchanged to evaluate, and is never part of cache identity. ClockProtocol.now()->int returns evaluator-controlled epoch seconds. ttl_seconds must be a non-boolean integer 1..3600; invalid ttl_seconds makes create_app raise ValueError before creating an app. POST /authorize accepts exact body tenant,subject,resource_id,action; canonical IDs/actions match ASCII [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}; revision and clock values are non-boolean integers 1..9223372036854775807. For each tenant/subject, a revision identifies immutable policy content, is never reused for different decisions, and strictly increases when policy changes. Request processing order is fixed: validate body without callbacks; call snapshot exactly once; validate the snapshot; call clock exactly once; validate the clock; perform lookup; on a miss call evaluate exactly once with the unchanged snapshot. If body validation fails no callback is called; if snapshot raises or is invalid, clock/evaluate are not called; if clock raises or is invalid, evaluate is not called; if evaluate raises or returns a non-boolean, no entry is created. On a miss the app caches either allowed=true or allowed=false; on a hit it calls evaluate zero times and returns the stored decision. Success is exact 200 {allowed:boolean,policy_revision:int,cache:'hit'|'miss'}; controlled failure is exact 422 {detail:'invalid_request'} and creates no cache entry. Cache entries expire when now-created_at >= ttl_seconds; an expired lookup evaluates again and replaces the entry without sliding expiry on hits. The cache is process-local.
replacement_candidate.qualification_control: Evaluator supplies synchronous in-memory PolicyStoreProtocol and ClockProtocol implementations with public snapshot/evaluate/clock call counters, mutates immutable strictly increasing policy snapshots only between completed public requests, varies exactly one cache-key dimension per guard, and observes only POST /authorize responses and those public counters. snapshot returns a newly allocated PolicySnapshot with a newly allocated identity-distinct evaluation_token on every call, including repeated snapshots at the same revision with unchanged evaluate semantics; same-revision exact repeats must still hit, so PolicySnapshot/token identity, equality, and hash cannot substitute for revision in cache identity. Every common control, scored guard, and near-miss probe uses a newly created app, store, clock, counters, and empty cache. Every implementation and mutant must pass all common_cache_controls; failure of a common control rejects the implementation independently of the five-check matrix.
private_static_reasoning_rubric: identify every security-relevant dimension before defining cache identity
include immutable policy revision in the key and enforce deterministic half-open TTL expiry
do not repair by disabling cache or always reporting misses

public_interface.input_contract: exact canonical tenant, subject, resource_id, action request and importable frozen policy interfaces defined by normative_profile
public_interface.state_or_output_boundary: callback order and counts follow normative_profile; evaluate exactly once on miss and zero times on hit; complete-key entries retain both allowed and denied decisions; invalid requests do not alter cache
public_interface.failure_contract: controlled validation or policy rejection preserves cache state and returns the exact documented error

common_cache_controls.contract: Before expiry, exact repeated allowed and denied requests each produce miss then hit, identical decisions/revisions, and exactly one evaluate call per pair.
common_cache_controls.purpose: Reject always-miss, cache disabling, allow-only caching, deny-only caching, flush-on-every-request, and fabricated hit labels.

common_cache_controls.contract: With ttl_seconds=60 and fill at t=100, an exact repeat at t=159 is a hit with no evaluation and an exact repeat at t=160 is a miss with one new evaluation.
common_cache_controls.purpose: Prove retained cache use and deterministic half-open expiry.

common_cache_controls.contract: Malformed requests, invalid snapshots, invalid clock values, and non-boolean evaluate results return exact invalid_request, create no entry, and cannot be turned into a later hit.

anti_duplication.singleflight-scope-key: This task measures retained authorization decisions reused across completed sequential requests and invalidated by immutable policy revision/TTL; singleflight measures concurrent in-flight computation coalescing. Passing either does not imply the other.
anti_duplication.version-fenced-read-cache: This task caches boolean policy decisions keyed by principal/action/revision context; version-fenced-read-cache caches resource representations fenced by durable data versions. Passing either does not imply the other.
anti_duplication.attenuated-capability-verifier: This task binds reuse of computed decisions to complete context; attenuated-capability-verifier proves delegated signed authority only narrows. Passing either does not imply the other.

checks.public_contract: A cached decision for one resource never authorizes a distinct concrete resource.
checks.planned_mutant: omits resource_id from the cache key
checks.planned_probe: Run two fresh-app subcases: prime allowed doc-a/read then denied doc-b/read; and prime allowed report/read then denied report.copy/read. In each, tenant, subject, revision, action, and time remain equal; the distinct request must miss/evaluate/deny and its exact repeat must hit without evaluation.

checks.public_contract: A decision is isolated by exact tenant identity.
checks.planned_mutant: omits tenant from the cache key
checks.planned_probe: Prime allow in tenant-a, then request the same subject/resource/action denied in tenant-b at equal revision.
checks.failure_atomicity: denied decisions do not affect other tenants

checks.public_contract: A decision is isolated by exact subject identity.
checks.planned_mutant: omits subject from the cache key
checks.planned_probe: Prime allow for alice, then request the same tenant/resource/action denied for bob at equal revision.
checks.failure_atomicity: denied decisions do not affect other subjects

checks.public_contract: A decision is isolated by exact action.
checks.planned_mutant: omits action from the cache key
checks.planned_probe: Prime allowed read, then request denied delete for the same tenant, subject, resource, and revision.
checks.failure_atomicity: a denied action does not poison an allowed action

checks.public_contract: A decision from one policy revision is never reused after the policy snapshot revision changes.
checks.planned_mutant: omits policy revision from the cache key
checks.planned_probe: Prime allow at revision 7, replace the same tenant/subject snapshot with revision 8 denying it, then repeat before TTL expiry.
checks.failure_atomicity: invalid replacement snapshots do not enter cache
